reason: Conversation 2 asked efficient, relevant questions (which zone, hob type), then correctly framed the fault as element-or-control that needs an engineer to test before any parts are bought, matching the ground truth's genuine uncertainty and safety boundary. Conversation 1 opened with an irrelevant induction/child-lock tangent, then looped the same 'I need the full model number' reply three times after the customer twice said they couldn't find it, ignored the useful 'display shows level but no glow' detail, never asked about prior slow heating, and steered toward self-ordering a replacement part without recommending an engineer. Conversation 2 is terse and ends somewhat abruptly, but it serves the homeowner far better on safety, honesty and escalation.
